extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent practitioners, and applicants submitting or evaluating affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 (AIA)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and evaluating affidavits or declarations under 37 CFR 1.130 to disqualify disclosures as prior art under AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b). Covers applicability, required content, evidentiary sufficiency, procedural limits, form paragraphs, and exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of 37 CFR 1.130
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a mechanism to file an affidavit or declaration to disqualify a disclosure as prior art by establishing that (a) the disclosure was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or (b) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor, or (for 1.130(b)) that the subject matter had been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor (or someone who obtained it from them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.130 is used to attempt to render a reference unavailable as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) by invoking the exceptions in 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1) and 102(b)(2). Compliance entitles the evidence to be considered but does not guarantee withdrawal of a rejection as a matter of right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability — AIA first-inventor-to-file scope
rubrics_metrics.description: This MPEP section and 37 CFR 1.130 apply to applications subject to the AIA first-inventor-to-file provisions (effective filing dates on or after March 16, 2013).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pre-AIA situations, analogous affidavits/declarations are handled under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132 and MPEP §§715–718/716.10. Use the appropriate rule depending on the application's effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130(a) — Attribution (when to use)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.130(a) may be submitted when a claim is rejected to show that a disclosure (or portion thereof) relied on as prior art was made by the inventor or a joint inventor or that the subject matter was obtained from the inventor or a joint inventor (pertaining to 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) and 102(b)(2)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to convert a fact pattern where the authorship/ inventive entity appears different into one where the reference originated with the applicant's inventive entity, subject to restrictions (see 'inappropriate situations').

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.130(b) — Prior public disclosure (when to use)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.130(b) may be submitted to show that the subject matter disclosed had, before such disclosure, been publicly disclosed by the inventor or a joint inventor or by another who obtained the subject matter from the inventor or joint inventor (pertaining to 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(B) and 102(b)(2)(B)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit/declaration under (b) must identify the subject matter and provide the date of public disclosure; if the earlier disclosure was a printed publication, a copy must accompany the submission; otherwise sufficient descriptive detail is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal limitation — one-year grace period
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.130 is not available to except disclosures that were made more than one year before the effective filing date of the claimed invention; such disclosures are prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check effective filing date per MPEP §2152.01. There are nuanced availability rules for 102(a)(2) references that were effectively filed earlier but published later; consult MPEP §2155.06 and §2154.01 et seq. as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inappropriate situations — derivation from a U.S. patent/application claiming the same
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.130 is not appropriate where the rejection is based on a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication that claims an invention that is the same or substantially the same as the applicant’s claimed invention and the affidavit/declaration contends an inventor named in that U.S. patent/application derived the claimed invention from the inventor named in the application under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the applicant or patent owner should file a petition for a derivation proceeding under 37 CFR 42.401 et seq. 1.130 may still be available if the reference is a non-U.S. document, or if the affidavit does not allege derivation but instead alleges public disclosure or attribution consistent with 102(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: When affidavits/declarations are not required (overlap of inventive entity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) is not required when the public disclosure, subject to 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A) exceptions, is by one or more joint inventors or the entire inventive entity of the application and does not name anyone else (i.e., it is obviously a grace-period disclosure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: application names A,B,C; publication names A,B and is within one year — the publication should not be applied in a 102(a)(1) rejection. Similarly applies when a patent document's inventive entity is a subset of the application inventive entity and is within the relevant period.

rubrics_metrics.name: When affidavits/declarations are not required (specification identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(a) is not required if the specification of the application under examination already identifies the disclosure or subject matter as having been made by or originating from one or more members of the inventive entity (see 37 CFR 1.77(b)(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the specification clearly states the origin of the disclosure as from the inventive entity, the examiner should treat the reference accordingly without a separate 1.130 submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — whether disclosure is subject to statutory exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel must determine whether the disclosure addressed in the affidavit/declaration is subject to the exceptions of 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A)/(B) or 102(b)(2)(A)/(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the disclosure falls outside those statutory exceptions (e.g., disclosed >1 year before effective filing date), the 1.130 affidavit/declaration is not available to disqualify the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — sufficiency of facts (weight and character)
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration must show sufficient facts, in weight and character, to establish that (1) the disclosure was made by the inventor or a joint inventor, or (2) the subject matter disclosed was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include: an unequivocal statement from the inventor(s) accompanied by reasonable explanation for additional authors; corroborating contemporaneous documentation or declarations from other inventors; and careful scrutiny where contrary evidence exists (e.g., a contrary statement from another named author).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criterion — evidentiary indicators and anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'unequivocal' inventor/joint-inventor statement plus reasonable explanation may suffice absent contrary evidence; a mere statement without explanation may be insufficient where contrary evidence exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases: In re DeBaun (unequivocal statement accepted when accompanied by drawing/corroboration); Ex parte Kroger (mere declarations insufficient in face of contrary third-party author letter). Consider contemporaneous documents and corroboration per EmeraChem and related authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements and exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration must meet formal requirements (see MPEP §717.01(c)); while 37 CFR 1.130 does not always require original exhibits like 37 CFR 1.131(b), when additional evidence is necessary the exhibits must accompany the affidavit/declaration, and an applicant must include any exhibits they wish to rely upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reliance is placed on a printed publication, include a copy. If non-printed prior public disclosure is alleged, describe the subject matter with sufficient detail and particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration must be timely presented; untimely submissions may be disregarded or deemed ineffective (see MPEP §717.01(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure filing dates are within deadlines and consistent with procedural requirements for the prosecution stage involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enabling-disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no requirement that an affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130 demonstrate that the inventor-originated disclosure was an 'enabling' disclosure within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 112(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute/ rule focuses on origin and timing rather than enablement; enablement issues remain separate (see MPEP §2155.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case evidentiary analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence necessary to show that a disclosure originated from the inventor or a joint inventor requires case-by-case analysis depending on whether the disclosure itself or the application specification makes origin apparent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determination is similar to the process for disqualifying a publication as not by 'others' (MPEP §2132.01) but with the lesser showing required by 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(1)(A). Consult MPEP §§2155.01 and 2155.03 for detailed analysis guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect if affidavit/declaration is effective
rubrics_metrics.description: If effective, a 37 CFR 1.130 affidavit/declaration will render the addressed disclosure unavailable as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a) and therefore unavailable for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 103 that rely on that disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the affidavit/declaration is effective, the reference may still be used for nonstatutory or statutory double patenting analyses, to show level of ordinary skill, or as evidence relevant to enablement inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph content and use (7.67.aia and 7.68.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the MPEP form paragraphs when indicating an affidavit/declaration is effective (7.67.aia) or ineffective (7.68.aia). Required bracketed insertions include: type (affidavit/declaration), subsection (a)/(b), filing date of the affidavit/declaration, affected claim(s), specific reference, and explanation of how the affidavit/declaration does or does not satisfy 35 U.S.C. 102(b) exception elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.67.aia must be preceded by 7.03.aia. When using 7.68.aia, include the statutory grounds and explanation of insufficiency. Populate brackets carefully (see list of bracket meanings in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit/declaration cannot alter prior art publication date for purposes of defeating other references
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful affidavit/declaration (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.132) establishing derivation by an author/patentee/applicant of a first reference does not permit the applicant to assume that author's/patentee's/applicant's publication date for the first reference so as to defeat a later second reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Costello: establishing derivation of an earlier reference does not let applicant 'step into the shoes' of that author with regard to the earlier publication date to negate other prior art.
